thread.title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) shares have been bought by Billionaire Warren Buffett

author: Jill King
title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) shares have been bought by Billionaire Warren Buffett
text:
May 6, 2018 Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) shares have been bought by Billionaire Warren Buffett
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) shares have been bought by Billionaire Warren Buffett, and on Saturday he suggested that he would acquire even more shares at the right price.
At the annual shareholder meeting of Berkshire Hathaway Inc’s, Buffett credited Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) with developing “extremely sticky” products to which consumers become attached and endorsed Apple Inc’s decision to repurchase its own stock, by saying that it was the technology company’s most productive use of cash.
“We would love to see Apple go down in price,” Buffett said. Berkshire is now Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s third largest shareholder, behind Vanguard Group and BlackRock Inc.
“I’m delighted to see them repurchasing shares,” Buffett said, just two days after he revealed having bought 75 million additional Apple Inc shares, and four days after Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) said it may repurchase $100 billion of stock. At the end of 2017, Berkshire had owned 165.3 million shares.
“I love the idea of having our 5 percent, or whatever it is, maybe grow to 6 or 7% without our laying out a dime.”
In a statement to CNBC, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s CEO Tim Cook said the company is “thrilled to have Warren and Berkshire as a major investor.”
“On a personal level, I’ve always greatly admired Warren and have always been grateful for his insight and advice,” Cook said.
As of Thursday’s closing price of $176.89 per share, Berkshire’s Apple stake was worth about $42.5 billion. Berkshire is now the third largest Apple shareholder, behind Vanguard and BlackRock.
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) also hit an all-time high Friday morning after Buffett’s revelation.
“It is an unbelievable company,” Buffett says. “If you look at Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), I think it earns almost twice as much as the second most profitable company in the United States.” About Jill King
